raw: | `mxcli lint --format json \| jq .` fails with `Invalid numeric literal at line 1`; `--format sarif > results.sarif` writes a corrupt file. stdout begins `Connected to: …` / `Loading cached catalog…` / `✓ Catalog ready` before the payload | The executor is constructed with `executor.New(os.Stdout)` via `newLoggedExecutor`, so every progress line shares the stream the payload is written to. Independent of which formatter runs — the chatter is emitted during connect and catalog build, before the formatter is reached | `cmd/mxcli/output_stream.go` (`isMachineReadableFormat`, `progressSink`), `cmd/mxcli/main.go` (`newLoggedExecutorTo`), `cmd/mxcli/cmd_lint.go`, `cmd/mxcli/cmd_report.go` | Pick the executor's writer from the resolved format: stderr when stdout carries a machine-readable payload (json/sarif/html/markdown), stdout otherwise. Route to **stderr, not io.Discard** — the progress is wanted on a terminal and in CI logs, it was merely on the wrong stream. `mxcli report` needs the extra condition that `-o <file>` frees stdout, so progress goes back to stdout there. Text mode must be left alone; assert that, or the fix silently degrades interactive use. Two commands share this because both build a catalog before formatting; any future command that prints a payload to stdout needs `progressSink` too. Issue #904 (residue) |
